subject: Architecture
title: The Flatiron: New York's Oddest Tower
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Flatiron: New York's Oddest Tower.

hook.text: In 1902, a 22-story triangle appeared at the intersection of Broadway and Fifth Avenue.

buildup.text: The Flatiron Building was only six feet wide at its narrow end — critics said wind would topple it.

discovery.text: Its steel frame made the narrow shape possible. Stone walls that thin would have crumbled instantly.

twist.text: Wind swirling around the building lifted women's skirts. Police had to patrol the intersection.

climax.text: Photographers loved its dramatic shape. It became the most photographed building in early New York.

punchline.text: Too thin to stand? It's been standing for over 120 years.

quiz.question: Why did critics doubt the Flatiron Building would survive?
options: Its foundation sat on unstable marshland
They believed wind would topple such a narrow structure
